schema_description: Versioned, append-only list of candidate benchmark/specification adjudications. See docs/research_protocol.md for the full adjudication policy and docs/pilot_findings.md for the narrative write-up of adjudication #1. This is a small tracked data file, not a database: new entries are appended by hand/script as candidates are adjudicated; existing entries are never edited or removed once recorded.

field_schema.candidate_id: string (UUID) -- generated candidate artifact id, or null for a tracked (non-generated) reference candidate
field_schema.candidate_source_sha256: string (hex sha256) -- hash of the exact candidate source that was reviewed and hidden-tested
field_schema.benchmark_pass: boolean -- whether ALL hidden tests passed, as mechanically measured by experiment.runner.PytestRunner; never edited to fit an outcome
field_schema.specification_correct: boolean -- human judgment: does the candidate's actual behavior on the disputed case(s) satisfy the written specification.md
field_schema.adjudication: string enum -- one of: valid_pass, valid_failure, benchmark_mismatch, ambiguous (see docs/research_protocol.md)
field_schema.mean_confidence_by_condition: object {A_NO_RESULT, B_VISIBLE_PASS, C_ADVERSARIAL} -- mean reviewer confidence (0-100) across repetitions, recorded before hidden tests were run
field_schema.evidence: object -- concise, specific evidence for the adjudication (failing inputs, a short specification quote, one-line reasoning); never full hidden-test source, never an API response id, never an absolute filesystem path
field_schema.excluded_from_primary_analysis: boolean -- true if this candidate is excluded from the primary semantic-correctness/calibration analysis (adjudication in {benchmark_mismatch, ambiguous})
field_schema.exclusion_reason: string or null -- one-line reason when excluded_from_primary_analysis is true, else null
field_schema.notes: string -- short free-text pointer to a fuller write-up, if one exists

failure_clusters: Circular/mutual dependency resolution (2/2 failing hidden tests): A<->B and A->B->C->A
evidence.failing_behavior: candidate raises ValueError('circular dependency') for A<->B and A->B->C->A instead of resolving them (each package already resolved before the back-reference is encountered)
evidence.specification_reference: specification.md Sec. 7: circular dependencies must report status="conflict"; docs/research_protocol.md 'Known task-specific ambiguities' documents that a mutual reference to a package already fully resolved before the back-reference is encountered may instead be a valid non-conflicting resolution, and mandates classifying such failures ambiguous.
evidence.reasoning: Both failing hidden tests are exactly the documented mutual-reference/already-resolved cycle case. No valid_failure exists, so the protocol's own circular-dependency ambiguity rule governs (post-data precedence rule 3).

adjudications.exclusion_reason: ambiguous: both failing hidden tests are the protocol's documented mutual/already-resolved circular-dependency case, with no other failure cause

failure_clusters: NaN/Infinity/-Infinity literal rejection (3/5 failing hidden tests) -- same benchmark_mismatch pattern as Q0/pilot
Unpaired surrogate acceptance (2/5 failing hidden tests): parse('"\\uD800"') and parse('"\\uDC00"') return a bare surrogate code point instead of raising
evidence.specification_quote: No Infinity, NaN, or hex. / Surrogate pairs: \uD800-\uDBFF followed by \uDC00-\uDFFF encode characters above U+FFFF.
evidence.reasoning: The spec explicitly forbids NaN/Infinity (contradicted by 3 hidden tests) but only describes valid surrogate pairs -- it never states what to do with a lone/unpaired surrogate, so that half of the failure is genuinely underspecified. Because at least one failure is ambiguous and none is a clear specification violation, post-data precedence rule 3 yields ambiguous, not benchmark_mismatch.

adjudications.exclusion_reason: ambiguous: failures mix an explicit NaN/Infinity specification contradiction with underspecified unpaired-surrogate handling; no clear specification violation exists

failure_clusters: Prerelease-vs-stable sort crash (1/4 failing hidden tests): TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'list' and 'NoneType' when comparing lib 1.0.0-alpha against lib 1.0.0
Circular/mutual dependency resolution (2/4 failing hidden tests) -- same documented ambiguity as Q1
Optional dependency that would conflict (1/4 failing hidden tests): returns conflict instead of skipping the conflicting optional dependency
evidence.specification_quote: Prefer latest: among compatible versions, always pick the highest. / Pre-release versions have lower precedence than the associated release version (1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0).
evidence.reasoning: The candidate's version-sort key mixes a list (prerelease identifiers) and None (no prerelease) and crashes with TypeError instead of comparing 1.0.0-alpha < 1.0.0 and picking the stable 1.0.0 release, directly violating the specification's explicit prefer-latest/prerelease-ordering rule. Per post-data precedence rule 2, this independently clear specification violation determines the candidate's category regardless of the additional ambiguous circular-dependency and optional-conflict failures.

failure_clusters: NaN/Infinity/-Infinity literal rejection (3/5 failing hidden tests)
Numeric overflow to +-inf (2/5 failing hidden tests): parse("1e309") and parse("-1e309") raise ValueError('number is not finite') instead of returning +-inf
evidence.specification_quote: No Infinity, NaN, or hex. (numeric grammar defines int/frac/exp for a number token; it does not state what to do when a well-formed token overflows IEEE-754 double range)
evidence.reasoning: The NaN/Infinity trio contradicts the explicit no-Infinity/NaN-token rule. Separately, 1e309/-1e309 are well-formed number tokens under the numeric grammar; the specification never states what a parser should do when such a token overflows IEEE-754 double range, so that failure is genuinely underspecified. At least one ambiguous failure and no clear violation means post-data precedence rule 3 applies.

adjudications.exclusion_reason: ambiguous: failures mix an explicit NaN/Infinity specification contradiction with underspecified numeric-overflow handling; no clear specification violation exists
